query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Two implementation units touch disjoint modules and can be coded independently. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge remain. Decide what may run in parallel and who owns integration.
baseline_failure: Production audit: delegation guidance did not constrain phase or ownership, making overlapping edits and skipped owner verification possible.
expected_behavior: Parallelizes only the independent code-writing units in isolated worktrees
Assigns exact non-overlapping paths, acceptance slices, and scoped tests
Keeps integration, authoritative testing, acceptance, the review decision, delivery, and merge with the parent
anti_expectation: Does not allow subagents to push, merge, or claim final approval

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: parallelizes architecture and code review, delegates unit ownership beyond writing, and proposes two PRs merged together

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced; implementation-only parallelism and single-parent integration are load-bearing

green_check.measured_against: `run/SKILL.md` plus `run/references/placement.md` as shipped at the commit that narrowed 'never parallelise review' to the review decision (finding 14), and re-checked after the later CONTEXT.md wording fix to the same file. Method: isolated haiku probes, as for the other eight.

runs.note: parallelises only the two code-writing units in isolated worktrees; keeps testing, acceptance, the review decision, delivery and merge with one integration owner -- 'no split verdict authority'
same shape, in the narrowed vocabulary: 'sequential: testing, acceptance, delivery, and review decision ... own the single review decision'

green_check.stability_caveat: Re-sampled at n=6 on 2026-08-21 this reproduced 2 of 6, and 3 of 6 against the previous revision of the same file -- so the variance is the probe, not the edit. The runs above are representative of the passing samples and are NOT a claim that it reproduces every time. The failing samples drift the same way each time: they parallelise unit testing or acceptance, or propose one PR per unit. See finding 16 in the eval log; the scenario is kept because its RED baseline is load-bearing and its GREEN is real when it lands, not because the rate is good.
